Building a new system for basically changing how we think about code coverage. Um and you know, he had the high-level idea and you know, got an agent to go off and implement it. And

Yep. And there's a real question of like, what do we want to understand and at what level? People often bring up the compiler as a kind of analogy in the space of like it used to be back in the ancient days, people would like write programs in machine code or assembly code, and then there were compilers and people stopped doing that and it was okay. And I think that's like both like a good and a bad analogy in the sense that like it it correctly highlights that we don't need to maintain understanding of every level of the system in the way that we did in the past. It's possible to go from one level to another and to be okay with it.
And also, boy are these things not compilers.
Yeah, like they're not deterministic.
They are not deterministic, they are hard to predict, they do weird stuff. They do weird stuff at every level.

It did a great job. Like, of the seven exercises, it rendered them all perfectly well, except for the one at the bottom where it had the arms coming out of the floor.
It was like, wow, that's like a mistake a human would never in a million years have made. Um, and I feel like that same kind of like arms coming out of the floor thing happens in the code too.
Yep.

And certainly in the current regime where we're in, human understanding is as critical as ever, kind of the whole way through. Like you can't really trust the models to do any piece of it without you understanding it. Right. Um, so I think it's really essential to figure out how to use the models as tools for human understanding. And and I do I feel like people do this. Like I hear, you know, I've talked to people who talk about how code review has gotten easier because you can use the models to help answer questions. Like you go through and you see if like why why did we why did the person do that? Like what about the API would make that happen? And of course, there are still hallucinations. There's less, but they're still there.

The explanation might be confidently wrong. Of course, if you tell the model that it's wrong, it'll be like, I'm so sorry. You're totally right. It's very compliant, but it does make mistakes. And yet, I think it can be a really powerful tool for understanding.
